page: The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for environments requiring single-tenant isolation, direct hardware access, and high single-core frequencies. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a six-core, twelve-thread Intel Xeon E-2286G processor operating at a 4.0 GHz base clock speed. The processor features 12 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets including AVX, AES, and bit-manipulation extensions. The system is provisioned with 32 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.67 GB per virtual thread, and includes a bundled 1920 GB local SSD storage array. No dedicated GPU hardware is installed, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded data manipulation throughput, placing in the top quartile for gzip compression at 35.51 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.91 GB/sec. PassMark memory testing also registers in the upper tenth percentile. Conversely, the platform exhibits constraints under wide memory access patterns, where uncached 256 MB block memory reads (32.51 GB/sec) and writes (14.71 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile. Similarly, compute throughput on wider parallel loads such as medium-sized 7B LLM token generation (7.38 tokens/sec) remains in the lower quartile, whereas general multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench scores remain within the median range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers dedicated physical hardware and an integrated 1.92 TB SSD without the virtualization overhead of multi-tenant environments. However, the limited 32 GB memory ceiling and restricted uncached memory bandwidth represent trade-offs against larger multi-socket platforms. Workload profiles that align best with the vbm-6c-32gb include transactional databases requiring isolated SSD storage, build and CI/CD pipelines leveraging high clock speeds, static web serving, and mid-tier software compilation tasks.
description: The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb is a bare-metal server featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon E-2286G processor with 6 physical cores and 12 threads running at 4.0 GHz. Designed for single-tenant compute without hypervisor overhead, it includes 32 GB of RAM and 1920 GB of local SSD storage, with no integrated GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-thread performance, demonstrating upper-quartile throughput in single-threaded compression tests and strong memory response benchmarks. However, the architecture shows lower-quartile throughput in large uncached memory bandwidth operations and intensive machine learning tasks. With its dedicated storage footprint and fast core clock rate, the server fits web serving, compilation, CI/CD runners, and transactional database services.
